learnings.statement: enumerate-blocks can enumerate HIDDEN (visible:false) component sub-parts as State blocks — e.g. a component's footer/topbar/extra-item variants the design instance hides. Figma REST image export returns null for a hidden node (framePngMissing:true), and the node is absent from figma-extract's designSpec (spec-slice yields a THIN 0-node slice). There is no visible design target, so the honest disposition is BLOCKED with evidence; a pixel/delta measurement is impossible (a measured block requires an on-disk frame PNG).
learnings.evidence: Loop 5 (Sidebar Filter) block state-sorting-dropdown-footer = I133:9780;7901:13314 'Footer' [HIDDEN] (user-email row); images API => null; contract-check flags missing frame + thin slice; verdict-gate accepts BLOCKED+evidence and still returns PASS.

learnings.statement: In BROWSER_PROBE selectors, CSS :nth-of-type() counts by element TAG among siblings, not by class. A menu whose direct children mix element roles (e.g. two group <div>s separated by a divider <div>) will have `.group:nth-of-type(2)` silently match the divider (2nd div) and miss the real 2nd group (3rd div), reporting the group's elements MISSING. Use explicit modifier classes (or :nth-child on a homogeneous child set), never `.class:nth-of-type(n)` across heterogeneous siblings.
learnings.evidence: Loop 5 content block: `.vcx-sort-group:nth-of-type(2)` matched the .vcx-sort-divider and flagged group-2 + its 2 values MISSING (gross element-count 7/10); switching to explicit .vcx-sort-group--filter fixed it to delta-clean.
